targetText: Thus, the questions of peace, we insist, are not questions reserved for the great powers. We, also, are concerned; we also have the right to be present in these negotiations.
explanation: Sankara challenges the imperialist assumption that global diplomacy and disarmament summits are the exclusive domain of major nuclear superpowers. Because modern conflicts and imperialist militarism impose severe economic, ecological, and geopolitical shocks onto underdeveloped nations, the peoples of the Global South have an existential stake in international peace negotiations and must not be treated as passive spectators.

targetText: Being a coveted object, it is only in the awareness [prise de conscience] of those who are really able to struggle for our unity, our development, our happiness and our liberation that we can avoid being the simple, manipulable pawns of imperialism.
explanation: Sankara emphasizes revolutionary consciousness (prise de conscience) as the essential shield against imperialist plunder. Africa possesses immense mineral, agricultural, and strategic resources that imperialist powers continuously seek to control. Without a collective political awakening and anti-colonial solidarity, African nations risk remaining client states subject to foreign manipulation.

targetText: we have to have the courage to condemn imperialism and to show in the clearest and simplest manner, the most acceptable manner for everyone, that imperialism exists, that it is trying to exploit us, to manipulate us, to use us. Our peace, and also peace in the world, all of this depends as well on peace in Africa.
explanation: Within multilateral bodies like the Organization of African Unity (OAU), neocolonial ties often silence critique due to diplomatic pressure or financial dependence. Sankara insists on ideological boldness: revolutionaries must plainly identify and denounce imperialist domination in broad international forums, connecting African continental liberation directly to global stability and anti-imperialist peace.

targetText: All this depends on our capacity to resist the exploitation they want to impose on us, on Africans, to resist the wars that they provoke in our homeland, the conflicts that they provoke between Africans, the military support, the bandits that they dispatch, the opposition groups that they arm for destabilizing progressive, revolutionary regimes.
explanation: This passage outlines the covert and proxy tactics of modern imperialism. Rather than direct colonial occupation, imperialist powers engineer inter-African regional conflicts, arm counter-revolutionary paramilitary factions, and install surveillance infrastructure to undermine progressive sovereign governments. Resisting these destabilization campaigns requires vigilant popular mobilization and self-defense.

targetText: The most important thing in the struggle that we are leading at the current moment in Burkina Faso is to raise awareness in each Burkinabe, man or woman, young or old, from the cities as from the countryside, that imperialism exists, that it is not simply a word, but that it is stalking us and wants to destroy us. This means an awareness that it is imperialism that is the principal factor responsible for our backwardness, and that we cannot build a happy society unless we agree to struggle against it.
explanation: Sankara locates the root cause of underdeveloped economies not in inherent local deficiencies or cultural traits, but in the structural violence and economic extraction of global imperialism. Popular socialist revolution requires demystifying imperialism for all working people, uniting urban workers and rural peasantry around a shared scientific understanding of the global capitalist forces that constrain national development.
